title: Basic types — quick overview
rememberThis: TypeScript has string, number, boolean, bigint — number is always IEEE 754 double (no decimal).
null (intentional) and undefined (missing) are two distinct types — enable strictNullChecks.
any disables checking; unknown requires narrowing; never is the bottom type for exhaustiveness.
Prefer literal unions and as const objects over enums for zero run-time cost and tree-shaking.
bullets: const infers literal types; let widens to string/number/boolean. Use as const to freeze objects.
void is for function returns you ignore; never is for impossible paths and exhaustive switches.
type for unions, tuples, and mapped types. interface for object shapes, extends, and declaration merging.
Numeric enums generate run-time objects with reverse mapping — validate deserialized values.
C# decimal → serialize as string or integer cents. C# enum → validate range in TypeScript.
All TypeScript types erase at compile time — validate JSON and API responses at boundaries.
